model.description: Deterministic in-memory adjacent-city campaign bot. It attacks one adjacent enemy city at a time per campaign day using campaign commands, preserves the protected source garrison, accepts a command-proposed reduced force when executable, and drives its side in battles with the deterministic tactical AI.
decisionRules: Select only directly connected cities owned by a non-allied, non-eliminated enemy faction; skip neutral cities and targets with active campaigns or battles.
Rank available attacks by defender-to-dispatched-force ratio, then nominal route days, source city ID, and target city ID.
Retain the existing 35%/1,000 protected source garrison rule and ten-officer campaign party cap.
Issue and answer campaign directives through executeV03Command; command route, alliance, food, officer, and resource checks remain authoritative.
Acknowledge due events before policy actions. Resolve the selected faction’s tactical turns with the deterministic battle AI and submit battle-day completion through the command boundary.

metricDefinitions.battleDuration: Tactical battle day number at the checkpoint; raw per-battle values are retained.
metricDefinitions.closeBattle: Resolved battle with an absolute surviving-troop difference no greater than 10% of combined initial troops.
metricDefinitions.relativeStrength: Initial attacker/defender troop counts and ratio; weaker-side wins are counted separately.
metricDefinitions.longDistance: Campaign route is multi-leg when the route snapshot includes an intermediate city; raw nominal route kilometres are retained.
metricDefinitions.governorIdle: Count only autonomous cities whose workMonthIndex matches the latest completed month; unobserved cities are kept separate.

victoryDefinitions.trueUnification: Every campaign city is controlled by the selected faction.
victoryDefinitions.hegemon: The engine declares victory after one faction controls Luoyang and at least 16 cities for 12 consecutive month boundaries, when no battle remains active. Reported separately from true city unification.

limitations: This is a narrow heuristic policy, not a human-like strategic agent: it does not prioritize economy, diplomacy, defense, raids/sacks, governance actions, long-term supply planning, or multi-front coordination.
It considers only direct adjacent enemy cities and uses a simple force-to-garrison ratio with nominal route time. Tactical battle outcomes are AI-driven, not human-play results.
It is an implementation diagnostic, not by itself a balance acceptance run; its policy biases the selected faction toward expansion and affects outcome distributions.
True unification, Hegemon claim/streak/win, player elimination, and the state winner are reported as distinct outcomes; this diagnostic does not establish feature completeness or gameplay quality.
It does not replace human campaign/battle playtests or a real low-end-device check.
